review_notes: Read the whole file, with Basic.lean for countJointSquarefree. Two repetitions stood out: the squarefree-to-finite-prime-conditions implication, and the real-valued error assembly (error_bound and crt_error_bound). I did not check the downstream users of these lemmas. The rewrites below have not been compiled.

findings.excerpt:
refine ⟨hNIcc, fun p _ => ?_⟩
  rw [Nat.squarefree_iff_prime_squarefree] at hSqN
  exact ⟨by rw [sq]; exact hSqN p p.prop,
findings.problem: The proof that a squarefree N with all b*N+d squarefree satisfies the prime-square non-divisibility conditions at every p ∈ S is written out twice, almost character for character. It converts via Nat.squarefree_iff_prime_squarefree, rewrites sq, and applies the hypothesis at p. The first copy is inside count_upper_bound_via_finite (lines 197–206). The second is the whole body of jointSquarefree_subset_finitePrime (lines 279–286). The statement of count_upper_bound_via_finite is exactly the cast of Finset.card_le_card applied to that subset lemma, after unfolding countJointSquarefree. So the real content is proved twice, and the two copies can drift apart.
findings.proposed_change:
Move jointSquarefree_subset_finitePrime above count_upper_bound_via_finite. It has the same hypotheses b T S X, so it needs no extra assumptions. Then prove count_upper_bound_via_finite as:
  rw [countJointSquarefree, Nat.cast_le]
  exact Finset.card_le_card (jointSquarefree_subset_finitePrime b T S X)
The subset lemma keeps its existing proof unchanged. The unused _hb and _hT arguments stay as they are. If `rw [countJointSquarefree]` fails to unfold under the cast, `unfold countJointSquarefree` or `show` can be used instead.
findings.benefit: The Nat.squarefree_iff_prime_squarefree unpacking is stated and maintained once. The upper-bound lemma becomes a two-line corollary of the subset inclusion. This also makes the lower-bound side, which already uses the subset lemma, and the upper-bound side visibly depend on the same fact.

findings.problem: error_bound (lines 127–142) and crt_error_bound (lines 227–241) state the same inequality. One writes the count as an unfolded `let` filter-card and the other uses countFinitePrime, which is that same expression by definition. Both prove it by the same chain: count_real_bounds, xL_real_bounds, localDensityProduct_nonneg, localDensityProduct_le_one, then final_error_bound. Each re-derives the sandwich bounds and the final assembly. error_bound also adds a by_cases on M = 0 and a separate lemma, error_bound_empty_case, only to handle a case that primeSquareProduct_pos rules out. crt_error_bound shows the case split is unnecessary: it uses primeSquareProduct_pos directly. It also has unused `let q` and `let count` bindings.
findings.proposed_change: Keep one proof, and make the other a corollary or delete it. Place countFinitePrime before error_bound, then prove crt_error_bound by the existing straight-line argument. It needs no case split, using primeSquareProduct_pos S for hM_pos. State error_bound as `intro M L count; exact crt_error_bound b hb T hT S X`, which should work because countFinitePrime unfolds to the `count` expression. Alternatively, drop error_bound and error_bound_empty_case and use crt_error_bound in count_finite_prime_approx via `unfold countFinitePrime`. Remove the unused lets.
findings.benefit: The count_real_bounds, xL_real_bounds, final_error_bound assembly appears once. The vacuous M = 0 branch and its helper lemma go away. A reader no longer has to check that two near-identical error bounds agree.
